feedback: Prompt the child to name both the sense and the organ each time: 'You heard the bird — with your…? Ears!'.
If a child uses only fingertips in the feely bag, invite them to try an arm or cheek to discover skin feels everywhere.
Affirm specific, real examples the child gives rather than generic praise.
activities.intendedInsight: The senses are real, first-hand experiences of your own body; doing them is intended to make the organ–sense link stick.
learnerActions: Smell something in a jar covered with a cloth or a lid with holes (orange, flower) using only your nose, then name the sense.
Explore a 'feely bag' of textures with your hands and also against your arm or cheek to show skin feels all over.
Go on a listening walk and name the sounds you hear with your ears.
Taste a tiny piece of food and notice what your tongue tells you.
After each activity, say which sense you used and which body part did the work.
activities.title: First-hand sense play (the real anchor)
